en.title: Airbnb OA #8: Round Prices to Hit a Target
en.description:
Given n prices prices=[x1,x2,…,xn] and a target value target, round each price to yi, where yi must be floor(xi) or ceil(xi), such that y1+y2+…+yn=target. Under this condition, minimize the rounding error Σ|xi−yi|. Output the rounded array.

The data guarantees that a valid and unique optimal result exists.
en.input: The first line contains two integers n and target; the second line contains n prices, each written with exactly two decimal places (such as 3.00 or 0.70). 1≤n≤100000, 0≤xi≤1000000.
en.output: Output one line of n integers y1..yn, separated by spaces.
en.explanation:
Example 1: prices=[1.20,4.30,5.80,6.40], target=18. The sum of floors is 16, so 2 of them must be rounded up instead; choosing 5.80 and 6.40, which have the largest fractional parts, gives [1,4,6,7] with an error of 1.3.
Example 2: prices=[0.70,2.80,4.90], target=8. The error of [0,3,5] is 0.7+0.2+0.1=1.0, which beats the 0.3+0.8+0.1=1.2 of [1,2,5].
Example 3: prices=[3.00,4.50,5.20,3.25], target=16. 3.00 is an integer, so rounding it up does not change it; the sum of floors is 15, so 1 more must be rounded up, and the largest fractional part belongs to 4.50, giving [3,5,5,3].
hints: Round everything down first and compute how much is still missing.
Changing one price from its floor to its ceiling changes the error by 1−2×(fractional part).
Parse the two-decimal prices as integers to avoid floating-point error.
